content_of_post_to_answer: How do you steer the interaction back to posing if a client gets too distracted by conversation?
answer: A useful distinction is that conversation itself is not always a distraction; sometimes it is part of building trust with the client. The challenge is knowing when the connection is serving the session and when it has replaced the purpose of the session. A gentle redirect works best when it acknowledges the person first: “I’d love to hear more about that, and I also want to make sure we capture the poses we planned today.” The best photographers don’t shut down conversation; they guide its rhythm. A client who feels heard is usually easier to direct than one who feels controlled.
